The gap between innovators and the first group of early adopters
The gap between the late majority and the laggards who resist change
The gap between established brands and brand-new startup companies
questions.why: Lesson 1 places the chasm between early adopters and the early majority, whose reasons for buying differ sharply.

questions.q: Why are pragmatic buyers reluctant to purchase from a high-tech newcomer?
a: They prefer proven products and established brands over big innovations
They want radical change and are happy to bet against the odds
They only buy products that have not yet been reviewed by anyone
They care mainly about getting the lowest possible price
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the early majority wants incremental improvements from proven products and established brands.

questions.q: According to the summary, how should a startup begin crossing the chasm?
a: Win over one very specific niche of the early majority first
Launch to the whole population at once to build momentum
Lower prices until every customer segment buys the product
Copy the marketing of the market leader in the same industry
questions.why: Lesson 2 recommends securing a narrow beachhead inside the early majority, then expanding from there.

questions.q: What advantage comes from selling only to one committed target segment?
a: It becomes easier to build a standard package that fits that group
It guarantees the product will never need any further changes
It removes the need to gather references or word of mouth
It lets the company skip positioning against any competitor
questions.why: Lesson 2 lists a smaller market, faster word of mouth and a standard package as benefits of focus.

questions.q: How can a newcomer position itself when no direct competitor exists?
a: Define the competition itself by contrasting with market and product alternatives
Wait until a direct competitor appears and then imitate its messaging
Describe every feature in detail rather than naming any comparison
Claim to be the cheapest option in every possible market
questions.why: Lesson 3 says you define your own competition using a market alternative and a product alternative.
